cues.en: We had a look at the dynamic component here, which provides a general skeleton for every post.
Kind of related to this is this special underscore layout component.
This is a reserved name, Underscore layout is a reserved name, whereas Svelte is or Sapper is looking
for.
And this defines a general layout into which you can embed your other pages.
So layout here on the root level, it's not in the blog folder, it's in the root routes level.
This is the layout which will be used for every page.
And this is useful for, for example, adding a nav bar to every page because you don't want to add
the nav bar manually to every page component here.
Instead, no matter which page we visit, if that's blog or about or home, we always have the same
nav bar.
Right?
And layout allows us to define this nav bar.
And then we have a slot here which actually holds the page component for index.
Well, here for svelte or for this index svelte.
So the content of these components gets rendered into the slot of the layout and that happens automatically.
And you need to have a slot here because that is what Svelte is looking for.
You may customize what happens around this slot though.
You can add your own footer, you can add your own nav bar, you can add your own styles for the main
section, whatever you need.
Error.
Svelte is another reserved name.
This is the error page, which svelte will return.
For example, if you enter an invalid URL.
If I enter slash blocks, I get the 404 error and that actually uses this template for this error page.
As I can prove if I add an error occurred as a text here.
If I do that and then I restart this npm run dev process, sometimes you need to do this, it should
reload automatically.
But in my experience you sometimes need to restart that.
So now if I restart that and I reload here you see an error occurred here.
So this is the error page, which is of course also useful for having a unique error handling technique
or a page which you simply can show to users if something goes wrong during server side rendering,
for example, because data can't be fetched or for example, because an invalid URL was entered.
